text:
christina: Heads-up: ran a daytime perf sweep against canary for continuous-batching tweaks and saw a regression on streamed responses after landing the new coalescer + KV eviction change. p50 up ~10ms, p95 spikes during concurrent small-chat workloads. logs + repro below.

omar: can you paste the exact config you toggled? and which kernel set was chosen when tails spiked?

christina: sure. baseline = master before coalescer change. experiment = coalescer-v2 + kv-ttl-evict-compact. observed: streaming flush cadence increased (more partial-decodes) because token_budget_target lowered from 256 -> 200 in the new heuristic, so smaller batches and earlier flushes. kernel handoffs increased due to more frequent short sequences, triggering small-kernel path swaps.

christina: repro steps:
```
# run workload: 300 concurrent streams, avg prompt len 60, response target 40 tokens
./bench --mode=stream --clients=300 --seq=100 --model=redwood-open-7b
# enable config:
continuous_batch: { enabled: true, token_budget_target: 200, max_batch_wait_ms: 8, min_batch_size: 2 }
kv: { prefetch_pct: 0.15, eviction_ttl_ms: 120000 }
```

christina: profiling snippets:
- sampler shows batch sizes median went 12 -> 6 tokens per batch
- kernel switch count per GPU went 4k/hr -> 9k/hr
- KV miss rate jumped 3.4% -> 7.9% on hot prefixes
- throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~12%

ben: this looks like two interacting regressions: smaller token budgets increase flush cadence which increases short-lived partial decodes; those partials don't amortize kernel load and they also miss KV warmups more often. small-kernel path has higher per-call overhead on our runtime.

anika: +1. I also saw the eviction_ttl change is evicting prefixes too aggressively. When a prefix is evicted and then immediately reused by a streaming client (partial decode), we pay both KV fetch + kernel reinit. For streaming that's doubly bad.

omar: good notes. quick hypothesis: raise token_budget_target back to 240 and increase max_batch_wait_ms to 12 to give coalescer more time to form useful batches for streams. Also bump prefetch_pct to 0.4 for streaming route only. Can we A/B that?

christina: testing now on canary-route-3 with those params. initial micro-try looks promising: median batch size recovered from 6 -> 10 and kernel switches fell ~35% in first 15m. will run longer.

ben: another mitigation: change queue policy so streaming low-latency clients are allowed slightly higher token_budget (policy weight), while best-effort clients keep the lower target. That keeps tail for streams stable.

anika: FYI infra-bot reported a deploy during the perf window: infra-bot: deploy-canary/2026-03-18T09:12 finished -> rolled coalescer-v2 to 6 nodes in region-1. might align with observed spikes.

christina: added a small experiment plan:
- A: token_budget_target=240, max_batch_wait_ms=12, prefetch_pct=0.4 (streaming routes only)
- B: revert token_budget_target to 256 for streams, keep coalescer-v2, raise eviction_ttl to 300k ms
- metrics to watch: p50/p95 stream latency, kernel_switch_count, kv_miss_rate, tokens/s

omar: sounds good. if A improves tail and keeps throughput, we can roll A to more nodes and schedule B as fallback. also let's add a short-term metric alarm if kernel_switch_count > baseline*2 in production.

ben: one more note — partial decode scheduling: consider delaying the first partial send by a few ms (early_send_hysteresis) when batch size < X to allow last-moment coalescing. saves a lot of tiny partials.

christina: good idea. I'll add early_send_hysteresis=4ms experiment as C.

anika: thanks. tagging @omar for follow-up on canary and I'll open a tiny PR to expose streaming-specific prefetch_pct.

omar: perfect. thanks team — keep updates in this thread with numbers. :thumbsup:
